decisions.reason: F1 claimed an S³ point-removal conclusion absent from its R³ supplier. Step 1.1 now chooses a point outside the embedded circle and uses an SO(4) rotation path to move that point to infinity before applying the regular-projection lemma. Rational approximation retains separated graph charts, transverse crossing sectors, orientations and crossing heights, and isotopy extension preserves the knot class. The Statement is unchanged; no consumer propagation is triggered.

The polygonal path of an edge can have a geometric bend in its interior; the algorithm expressly excludes such a basepoint. The repair retains every original basepoint by moving a bend basepoint a short distance forward within the same edge before the call. No crossing is passed, so crossing encounter order, the output labels and the crossing-change list are unchanged by this adjustment. Finiteness gives a nonbend choice and termination, including zero crossings.

The stated diagram domain omitted the one-component hypothesis required by the Seifert algorithm, embedded-surface supplier and knot Seifert-pairing definition. The Statement now explicitly says knot diagrams, matching the existing Given and intended knot-only contract. The unchanged common-graph proof chooses fundamental cycles avoiding the changed band except for one cycle; a full twist alters only that cycle’s diagonal pairing by ±1. This is a domain/citation defect rather than an invalid rank-one calculation.

The original step 4.1 did not establish a bridge-free separating disk, so its nesting and termination argument was unsupported. The repair explicitly imports Negami–Okita Lemma 3-3, m=2, under CLAUDE §12, checks essential-annulus and nonsplit hypotheses, and explains smooth disk-product realizations. Opposite-side punctures are now stated. This is source-backed repair, not independent verification of the imported innermost-arc proof.

The rationality objection is false: admissibility already includes a rational polygonal certificate and changing over/under labels preserves it. A separate domain defect was confirmed during this review: a geometric bend can lie inside a polygonal edge while the algorithm excludes bend basepoints. The repair uses the corrected traversal-properties theorem to move such a basepoint within its edge before the call, retaining every original input and the same crossing list. The descending output and finite c(D) bound then follow with all hypotheses met.
decisions.additional_defect: Algorithm input excludes geometric bend basepoints, which the original theorem allowed.

decisions.reason: The former supplier Statement guaranteed two puncture-to-circle arcs but omitted the opposite-side condition invoked in step 4.1; that condition is now explicit in the repaired supplier. The upper gluing gives the reverse inequality and the unknot identity covers trivial factors. The diagram now shows four distinct remaining bridge endpoints and the joined disks.
